notes:
Source is a macrobiotic (陰陽) page from G-veggie. It contains exactly one concrete food list, structured as 春夏向きの食べ物 (L44-48) vs 秋冬向きの食べ物 (L49-53). The direction mapping is stated by the source itself, not inferred by the coder: L21 defines 陰性の食べ物 = 冷やす力のある / 陽性の食べ物 = 体を暖める力のある, and L39-43 states 「春夏の気温が上昇するシーズンには『陰性の食べ物』、秋冬の気温が下降するシーズンには『陽性の食べ物』で料理をすること」. So 春夏向き list = 陰性 = cool, 秋冬向き list = 陽性 = warm. L26-31 (陰性の特徴: からだを冷やし、ゆるめる力がある) and L33-38 (陽性の特徴: からだを温め、引き締める力がある) reinforce this. 15 cool + 15 warm = 30 foods; no neutral attributions anywhere in the source.

JUDGMENT CALLS / FLAGS:
(1) 豆腐 is split by serving state: 豆腐（冷たい）under 春夏/陰性 (L47) and 豆腐（温かい）under 秋冬/陽性 (L52). I treated this as a §3 condition split (analogous to raw vs cooked ginger) rather than a 「冷たい飲み物」-type serving-temperature item, because 豆腐 is a real food and the source assigns each state a yin/yang nature via the list it sits in. Verbatim forms with full-width parentheses used. If the adjudicator prefers, these two rows could instead be demoted to serving_temperature_items.
(2) Group headers 穀物 / 豆類 / 豆の加工品 / 海藻 were NOT coded as umbrella categories, because each of the four appears in BOTH the 春夏 and the 秋冬 list (L45-48 vs L50-53). They are grouping row labels within a two-sided layout, not category-level attributions — coding 海藻 as both warm and cool would be a contradiction the source does not make. This differs from sources that assign a direction to a category itself.
(3) 「大きい豆（いんげん豆・花豆など）」(L46) coded as three rows: the umbrella 大きい豆 plus the two named examples いんげん豆 and 花豆, all cool.
(4) Nothing else in the page carries a direction. The rest is a 陰陽五行 season↔organ table (L62-68, organs not foods), teacher/school boilerplate (L70-85), and unrelated recipe-article teasers (L86-105) mentioning 大根/にんじん/ビーツ/バナナ/大豆ミート with no warm/cool attribution — ビーツ is only called 根菜 with nutrition claims, not a nature. No FAQ block, no captions with attributions.
(5) No serving-temperature items of the 「冷たい飲み物」 type appear in this source.
